claims.paper: §3.4 / §5.6 (shallow lakes' plants and water clarity; proposed addition, brief Phase 5)
claims.claim: over a range of nutrient levels shallow lakes can sit in either of two alternative states, clear and vegetated or turbid and algal
claims.note: abstract only. The abstract says 'shallow lakes can have two alternative equilibria: a clear state dominated by aquatic vegetation, and a turbid state characterized by high algal biomass', that nutrient reduction alone may do little for clarity while a disturbance such as food-web manipulation can return a lake to a stable clear state. Not confirmable from the abstract (rule 1); nothing quantitative (the nutrient range, the depths) can be taken from it
